name: Edmonton

portal.licence: City of Edmonton Open Data Terms of Use

growth_year_note: Homes built in or after 2021, the year of the last published Census. The 2026 Census population counts are scheduled for 10 February 2027.

wards.title: City of Edmonton Ward Boundary and Council Composition (Current)

homes.title: Property Assessment Data (Current Calendar Year)
homes.where_note: Residential and other residential (apartment) properties assessed at $40,000 or more; lower values are mostly parking stalls, storage units and remnant parcels.
homes.placement_note: each property placed at the point the City publishes for it
homes.unit: one assessed residential property (a house, a townhouse, a condominium unit or an apartment building)

unit_estimate.note: apartment buildings (other residential) count as their floor area divided by 85 m² per home (an estimate)

limitations: Apartment buildings are one account each; their homes are estimated from floor area.
Properties assessed under $40,000 are left out (mostly parking stalls and storage units).

census_plus_new.label: 2021 Census plus new homes
census_plus_new.title: Residents and children by neighbourhood: 2021 Census plus homes built since (estimate)
census_plus_new.about: Each neighbourhood's 2021 Census count, plus residents for homes built since 2021 at the neighbourhood's people per home (or the city's, for new neighbourhoods); children for new residents at the share seen in neighbourhoods mostly built in the ten years before the census.
limitations: An estimate: no population figure between Censuses is published by neighbourhood.

census2021.label: 2021 Census
census2021.title: 2021 Federal Census: Population
census2021.about: Each neighbourhood's 2021 Census count, unchanged. Neighbourhoods built since have little or no count.
limitations: Counts are as of May 2021; growth since is not included.
Statistics Canada rounds counts, so neighbourhoods may not add exactly to the city total.

Neighbourhoods renamed, renumbered or split since the census (for example Oliver, now Wîhkwêntôwin) are matched by the census-day boundary: their residents go to today's neighbourhoods in proportion to the homes inside it that were built before 2021.

boundaries.title: 2021 Federal Census: Neighbourhoods as of Official Census Day

playground.label: Playground
playground.title: Playgrounds
playground.threshold_basis: Platform choice: 400 m (about a five-minute walk) and 800 m (about ten minutes), the same as every city.
limitations: City-maintained playgrounds; school and other playgrounds come from OpenStreetMap where mapped.

park.label: Public park
park.title: Parks
park.where: status='Active' AND class not in('PUL','Unknown','Other Land Type')
park.threshold_basis: Platform choice: distance to the park's edge, 400 m and 800 m.
limitations: Active parks of every class, from pocket parks to natural areas and river valley parks.

crowding.unit: park hectares per 1,000 residents within reach

transit_stop.label: Transit stop
transit_stop.title: ETS Bus Schedule GTFS Data Feed - Stops
transit_stop.threshold_basis: Platform choice: 400 m and 800 m, the same as every city.
limitations: Bus and LRT stops in the current timetable; how often they are served is not measured yet.

crowding.unit: transit stops per 1,000 residents within reach

community_centre.label: Community league hall
community_centre.title: Community League Halls
community_centre.threshold_basis: Platform choice: 800 m and 1.6 km, the same as community centres in every city.
limitations: Community league halls as listed by the City; programs and opening hours are not measured.

rec_centre.label: Indoor recreation centre
rec_centre.title: Recreation Facilities
rec_centre.threshold_basis: Platform choice: 2 km and 5 km for facilities that serve several neighbourhoods.
limitations: City recreation, leisure and fitness centres (19); arenas, outdoor pools and sports fields are left out.

crowding.unit: indoor recreation centres per 100,000 residents within reach

readiness.data_availability: High for this module: neighbourhoods, wards, every residential property with location and year built, playgrounds, parks, transit stops, community league halls, recreation centres, libraries, 2021 Census by neighbourhood (age included). Also published: 311 requests, building and development permits, schools.
readiness.data_quality: High. Apartment buildings are one account each, so their homes are estimated from floor area (Calgary uses building permits). About 7,600 homes have no neighbourhood code on the roll and are placed by location. Four 2021 Census neighbourhoods have since been renamed or renumbered; their residents are placed by the census-day boundary.
readiness.geographic_compatibility: Neighbourhoods (about 400, including industrial ones) in 12 named wards. Neighbourhoods are not equivalent to Calgary's communities: compare cities only at the city level.
readiness.historical_coverage: Property roll: current year (year built gives the build history). 311 from 2014. Census 2021 by neighbourhood; municipal censuses 2009 to 2019.
readiness.indicator_comparability: The access, crowding and score measures use the same method, thresholds and rules as Calgary. Population differs: Calgary uses Calgary Data Desk's estimates, Edmonton the 2021 Census plus new homes. Scores are against each city's own level, so they are not comparable between cities; shares of homes within reach are.
readiness.update_frequency: Assets weekly; property roll yearly; census every five years.
readiness.not_yet: City dashboard figures (311, crime, permits, schools) are not built for Edmonton yet.
